question.problem:
A card is drawn at random from a standard $52$-card deck. What is the probability of drawing a number card greater than $7$ or a non-spade card?

*Hint: A standard $52$-card pack has four suits, each containing $13$ cards. Spades is one of these suits. Number cards are the cards labelled $2$ through $10$ in each suit. A jack, queen or king is not considered a number card.*
question.worked_solution:
Let's call $G$ the event "a card labeled with a number greater than $7$ is selected" and $N$ the event "a non-spade card is selected." 

The required probability is $P(G\cup N),$ which we can find using the addition law

$$
P(G\cup N)=P(G)+P(N)-P(G\cap N).
$$

Let's find $P(G)$ and $P(N).$

- There are $12$ cards labeled with a number greater than $7$ in a standard deck. So, we have

$$
P(G)=\frac{12}{52}=\frac{3}{13}.
$$

- There are $39$ non-spade cards in a standard deck. So, we have

$$
P(N)=\frac{39}{52}=\frac{3}{4}.
$$

- There are $9$ non-spade cards labeled with a number greater than $7.$ Indeed, the cards labeled with a number greater than $7$ are $8,$ $9,$ and $10,$ giving $3$ such cards per suit. Since there are $3$ non-spade suits, we have

$$
P(G\cap N)=\frac{9}{52}.
$$

Finally, substituting all of the known information into the addition law, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(G\cup N) & =P(G)+P(N)-P(G\cap N) \\  & =\frac{3}{13}+\frac{3}{4}-\frac{9}{52} \\  & =\frac{21}{26}.\end{aligned}
$$
